---
title: "Terramechanics Reference Data"
subtitle: "Measured soil tests for judging terramechanics simulations."
toc: false
---
This site provides laboratory soil tests as numbers: for example, the force needed to push a cylinder into sand as it goes deeper, or the stress at which a soil sample fails in shear. Each test comes with what one would need to set up the same test in a simulator (the soil, how its bed was prepared, the tool and how it moved), and states what the original report leaves out. Every number links to the page of the report it was read from.

This is the beginning of an effort to collect, curate and share well-documented test data that can be used to judge the simulation tools used in terramechanics. To that end, the site also shows how the data are meant to be used with an open-source simulator to gauge its accuracy.

For instance, one set of tests comes from a 1968 NASA study for the Apollo Lunar Module, in which twelve soil conditions were tested on Earth to predict how the lander's footpads would behave on the Moon.

The collection will grow with further tests, and contributions are welcome of two kinds: data from new physical tests, and scripts that run virtual experiments mirroring the physical tests hosted here.

## Start here

One test, from its setup to its citation: [[LPT]{.term title="load-penetration test: a tool is pushed into a soil bed and the load is recorded against depth" tabindex="0"} 24](experiments/b68-lpt-024.qmd), a 4-inch (102 mm) cylinder pushed into a bed of dense red scoria.

1. Its page gives the setup as a virtual experiment card: the soil, the bed, the tool and the motion, each value with the page it is printed on, and what the report leaves out.
2. Its points are in [observations.csv](files/data/experiments/b68-lpt-024/observations.csv): load against penetration in SI units, with the value as printed kept beside each one.
3. Each point carries a reading bound, how precisely it could be read off the printed figure (not the scatter of the experiment), and a status that says how it was checked; the [Glossary](glossary/index.qmd) defines both.
4. Each point traces to the scan: the [Figures](figures/index.qmd#check-f2-42) page draws the two readings over the printed figure, Fig. 2-42.
5. To cite it: the release by its DOI, and the record by its id and source page, for example record `b68-lpt-024`, AM-68-1 Vol. I, Fig. 2-42, printed 2-77, PDF 102 ([Download](downloads/index.qmd#how-to-cite) gives the entries).

[Simulate a test](simulate/index.qmd) walks through setting this test up in a simulator.

## In the collection

Measured data for 85 direct shear tests, 22 load-penetration tests, 11 sonic modulus tests, 3 dynamic penetrometer tests, 3 footpad impact tests and 2 drops of a 1/6-scale Lunar Module model, on these test soils:

| code | soil |
| --- | --- |
| [RS]{.term title="red crushed volcanic scoria, narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} | red crushed volcanic scoria, narrowly graded |
| [PS]{.term title="white crushed pumice, narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} | white crushed pumice, narrowly graded |
| [RSM-a]{.term title="RS mixed with crushed marble, 5 to 7 by weight, narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} | RS mixed with crushed marble, 5 to 7 by weight, narrowly graded |
| [RC2]{.term title="red crushed volcanic scoria, broadly graded" tabindex="0"} | red crushed volcanic scoria, broadly graded |
| [SS]{.term title="white silica sand (Wedron 4040), narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} | white silica sand (Wedron 4040), narrowly graded |
| [LSM]{.term title="broadly graded scoria (RC2) mixed with air-floated clay" tabindex="0"} | broadly graded scoria (RC2) mixed with air-floated clay |
| [RSM-b]{.term title="RS mixed with crushed marble, 1 to 3 by weight, narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} | RS mixed with crushed marble, 1 to 3 by weight, narrowly graded |
